newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebels advance towards Zaire's Shaba province.
newsitem.headline: Rebels advance towards Zaire's Shaba province.

text.p: Rebel fighters holding towns and territory in eastern Zaire are advancing towards the mineral-producing province of Shaba and Kalemie, home town of rebel leader Laurent Kabila, sources on both sides said.

Zaire's army earlier accused Uganda of sending several thousand troops into the east of the sprawling Central African nation to bolster rebel defences against its counter-offensive. Both Uganda and Rwanda denied the charge.

The Tutsi-led rebels, who launched their campaign last October, say they want to topple veteran President Mobutu Sese Seko, who is now in Europe for medical checks following cancer surgery last August.
"We have received information the rebels have taken the town of Lulimba southwest of Fizi," said a U.N. official in Rwanda's capital Kigali. Rebel radio later carried a similar report.
Lulimba, 60 km (40 miles) from Fizi, is only 30 km (20 miles) north of the border of Shaba province.

A Defence Ministry official in Kinshasa, who like the U.N. official declined to be identified, told Reuters a column of rebels was heading towards Shaba and had reached Lulimba, 130 km (80 miles) north of Kalemie.
He said Zairean soldiers had in the past few days retaken the western part of the strategic town of Bunia but Ugandan troops had intervened to bolster the rebels in the rest of the town.
He also said Zairean commandos recaptured the gold mining centre of Kamituga in South Kivu province last weekend.
He had no details of the fighting or casualties, but he said much of the information on incursions onto Zaire's territory came from military intelligence units operating in rebel-held areas.
A communique released by army headquarters in Kinshasa spoke of up to 8,000 Ugandan soldiers operating on Zairean soil.

"Along the Zaire-Uganda border the presence of 2,000 men transported in vehicles armed with machine guns has been reported. These men crossed over into Zaire after receiving petrol supplies from the Ugandan state," it said.
It said Ugandan troops with anti-aircraft missiles and thousands more Ugandan soldiers were operating between Goma in North Kivu province and Kalemie in Shaba.

There was no independent confirmation of the claim but diplomats in Kinshasa reported a significant build-up of troops inside the Ugandan border near Bunia and said more than 400 Rwandan troops had crossed from Rwanda to the area near Goma.
Zaire has signifigantly increased its arsenal in recent weeks, importing combat helicopters, fighter jets, artillery and munitions as well as around 300 foreign mercenaries.
Independent sources among the civil and diplomatic community said Zaire's army was counter-attacking on either side of Bunia and west and south of the South Kivu provincial capital of Bukavu.
Both the army and independent sources in radio contact with the region reported clashes near Bunia.
